hints: Focus on what Le Chatelier tells us, equilibrium shifts to oppose any change in pressure or temperature.
Count the moles of gas on each side, you have 1 + 3 on the left and 1 + 1 on the right, so think which pressure pushes toward methanol.
Notice that $\Delta H$ is negative, so the forward reaction gives out heat, think which temperature will favour the exothermic direction.
walkthrough:
**Count the gas moles to decide on pressure**

Think of pressure as squeezing the mixture. Equilibrium moves to the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce the pressure.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Left side = 1 + 3 = 4 moles of gas. Right side = 1 + 1 = 2 moles of gas. So high pressure shifts equilibrium to the right, giving more methanol.

**Use the sign of $\Delta H$ to decide on temperature**

Here $\Delta H = -49 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so the forward reaction is exothermic. It releases heat as it makes methanol.

Think of heat as a product:
$$\text{reactants} \rightleftharpoons \text{products + heat}$$
Lowering the temperature removes heat, so equilibrium shifts forward to replace it. That means a low temperature favours methanol yield.

**Combine both conditions for greatest yield**

For maximum methanol at equilibrium we want both shifts to work together.

High pressure favours the side with fewer moles. Low temperature favours the exothermic direction. So choose high pressure with the lower temperature, 20 degrees C.

options.A: High pressure is correct because it favours 2 moles on the right over 4 moles on the left, but 80 degrees C is too warm. For an exothermic forward reaction, higher temperature shifts equilibrium back to the left, so yield is lower than at 20 degrees C.
options.B: High pressure shifts equilibrium to the right where there are fewer gas moles (2 vs 4). Low temperature of 20 degrees C shifts equilibrium to the right because the forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H$ negative). Both effects maximise methanol yield.
options.C: This is the worst combination. Low pressure favours the left with more gas moles, and 80 degrees C favours the endothermic backward reaction. Both shifts reduce methanol yield.
options.D: 20 degrees C is correct for an exothermic reaction, but low pressure is wrong. Low pressure shifts equilibrium to the left toward 4 moles of gas, so much less methanol forms despite the good temperature.
